title: Short Stuff: War of Jenkins' Ear
summary: Short Stuff episode on the War of Jenkins' Ear (1739-1748), an 18th-century conflict between England and Spain. The hosts trace how the War of Spanish Succession and the Treaty of Utrecht set up trade rules that England, which was smuggling contraband, resented. Spanish coast guard boarding of the Rebecca, captained by Robert Jenkins, led to the ear-cutting story and Jenkins's testimony to Parliament. The hosts note the ear story is likely embellished and that the war was later absorbed into King George's War and the War of Austrian Succession. They cover the Battle of Bloody Marsh in Georgia and Oglethorpe's failed campaign against St. Augustine.

segments.title: Intro and overview
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the War of Jenkins' Ear and note it was named about a hundred and ten years after it happened, by Thomas Carlyle, and was really part of the War of Austrian Succession.

segments.title: Succession wars and the Spanish throne
segments.summary: Hosts explain how European royal succession disputes, starting with the death of Charles II of Spain without an heir, drew in France, Austria, Spain and England and led to the War of Spanish Succession.

segments.title: Colonial tensions and Treaty of Utrecht
segments.summary: Border skirmishes between Georgia and Spanish Florida grew out of the War of Spanish Succession. The Treaty of Utrecht allowed English trade with Spain, which the hosts say was really about English access to the Caribbean slave trade.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Hosts pause before the next part of the story.

segments.title: Smuggling and the Rebecca incident
segments.summary: English traders smuggled contraband into Spanish colonies, and Spanish coast guard boarded ships to search them. On April 9, the Spanish boarded the Rebecca, captained by Robert Jenkins. The Spanish captain Juan de Leon Fandino ordered Jenkins's ear cut off.

segments.title: Jenkins before Parliament
segments.summary: Jenkins carried the pickled ear for years and later testified before the House of Commons. Parliament declared war on Spain. The hosts say there is no evidence he actually showed the ear.

segments.title: Battles and legacy
segments.summary: The war was mostly small battles. The Battle of Bloody Marsh on St. Simon's Island saw Georgian defenders repel about 5,000 Spanish troops. Oglethorpe's campaign against St. Augustine failed. The war was absorbed into King George's War and the War of Austrian Succession.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts joke about the war-within-a-war structure and sign off, noting Ellen Page's upcoming appearance.
